spatial_claims.claim: C lies on segment AB between A and B, with AC being the greater segment (AC > CB). AB:AC = AC:CB (extreme and mean ratio).
D is the midpoint of AB, so D lies on segment AB with AD = DB = AB/2. The order on AB is A-D-C-B since AC > AB/2.
DE is a constructed line segment of length AC + DB (= AC + AD). By 13.1, sq(DE) = 5 * sq(DB), so DE = sqrt(5) * DB.
AC = DE - DB, expressing the greater segment as the difference of two constructed lengths. Requires DE > DB.
DF is a constructed line segment of length 3 * DB.
CB = DF - DE = 3*DB - sqrt(5)*DB, expressing the lesser segment as the difference of two constructed lengths. Requires DF > DE.

configuration_map: Points A and B define a rational straight line. C is on AB between A and B with AC > CB (golden ratio cut, AC/AB ~ 0.618). D is the midpoint of AB (AD = DB = AB/2); since AC > AB/2, the order on AB is A-D-C-B. DE is a separately constructed segment of length AC + DB = (AC + AB/2), which equals sqrt(5) * DB by Proposition 13.1. DF is a separately constructed segment of length 3 * DB. The proof works entirely through algebraic manipulation of these lengths, showing commensurability relationships via ratios of numbers (5:1 and 9:5) to establish that AC = DE - DB and CB = DF - DE are both apotomes by Proposition 10.73. No angles, circles, triangles, or spatial configurations beyond collinear points and lengths are involved.
pass_reason: The proof is primarily algebraic, operating through commensurability theory (Book 10) on line segment lengths. The few spatial claims (C and D on segment AB, constructed segments DE and DF) are all mutually consistent. Key consistency checks: DE = sqrt(5)*DB > DB (so AC = DE - DB > 0), DF = 3*DB > sqrt(5)*DB = DE (so CB = DF - DE > 0), and AC + CB = (DE - DB) + (DF - DE) = DF - DB = 2*DB = AB. No angle decompositions, no interior/exterior claims, and no geometric configuration contradictions exist.
